title: Personal Manifestation Video Maker · Visionflick
excerpt: Turn your goals into a short manifestation video: AI scenes, your affirmations spoken aloud, calm music. A daily ritual. Free storyboard, no subscription.
content_html:
Visionflick turns your goals into a short manifestation and visualization film: AI-created scenes, real video clips, your affirmations spoken by a calm voice, and music.

  • Choose from all areas of life
  • Use our affirmations or write your own
  • Real video clips, not just still images
  • Plan your film for free before you buy

Create your film Watch an example

Free storyboard · One payment, no subscription

A Vision Flick is a short film about the life you want: scenes of your goals, paired with your affirmations. Think of it as a vision board that moves and speaks. Watching it each morning is a simple way to keep your goals in front of you.

The film
Your goals, scene by scene, with real video clips that bring them to life.

The affirmations
Pick ready-made affirmations from our large library, sorted by area of life, or write your own.

The voice
Your affirmations, spoken aloud by one of four calm voices: Emma, Grace, James or Daniel.

The music
A calm soundtrack that sets the mood.

In motion

Many vision videos are slideshows of still photos. In your Visionflick, scenes come to life as short AI video clips, with Premium every single one: waves roll in, grass moves in the wind, the moment feels real.

The shift

Most goals live in a list that nobody reads. Visualization works with pictures, so your film shows your goals instead of listing them.

Goals in a notes app

My goals

• Wake up early and feel energized

• Find a bright new apartment

• Spend more time with friends

• Travel somewhere new this year

  • Just words on a screen
  • Read in silence, if at all
  • You have to imagine everything yourself
  • Feels like a to-do list
  • Easy to forget
  • Out of sight

Goals as a film

  • Scenes you can see
  • Your affirmations, spoken aloud
  • Images that help you picture it
  • Music that sets a calm mood
  • A short ritual each morning
  • On your phone, ready to play

  • See it

    Your goals turn into pictures, many of them in motion. You don't start from a blank page.

  • Hear it

    A calm voice speaks your affirmations, so the words reach you while you watch.

  • Feel it

    Music and images set the mood, so the moment feels like a small ritual, not a task.

What research says

Visionflick builds on well-studied findings about mental imagery and goals.

  • Pictures move us more than words.

    Imagining positive scenes lifted mood more than thinking about them in words.

    Holmes et al., Behavior Therapy, 2006 Holmes et al., Emotion, 2008

  • Pictures stay with you.

    We remember pictures better than words.

    Paivio & Csapo, Cognitive Psychology, 1973

  • A few minutes a day.

    Imagining your best possible future for five minutes a day raised optimism in studies. And in field studies, reminders that named a person’s own goal helped them stick to it. Generic reminders did not.

    Meevissen et al., J. Behav. Ther. Exp. Psychiatry, 2011 Carrillo et al., PLoS ONE, 2019 Karlan et al., Management Science, 2016

  • Imagining uses your visual brain.

    Imagining a scene uses many of the same brain systems as seeing it.

    Kosslyn et al., Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2001 Pearson, Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2019

  • Rehearsing in your mind.

    Mental practice can improve your performance.

    Pascual-Leone et al., J. Neurophysiology, 1995 Toth et al., Psychology of Sport and Exercise, 2020

  • Be specific, and picture the steps.

    Specific goals lead to better performance than a vague “do your best”. And imagining the steps helped students more than imagining only the result.

    Locke & Latham, American Psychologist, 2002 Pham & Taylor, Pers. Soc. Psychol. Bulletin, 1999

These studies looked at mental imagery and goals in general, not at Visionflick itself.

Step by step

  1. 01

    Choose your areas

    Pick one to 8 areas of your life.

  2. 02

    Pick or write your affirmations

    Choose from our library or write your own, in the first person.

  3. 03

    Shape your storyboard

    Swap any image, describe what a scene should show, and pick a voice.

  4. 04

    See a finished film, then get yours

    Before you buy, watch an example of a finished film. After you buy, your film is made and you can download it or share a link.

one-time

  • 10 scenes, 5 video clips
  • A new AI image for every scene you describe
  • Every affirmation spoken
  • Download and share link

Create your film

Every scene in motion

Premium

one-time

  • Everything in Standard, plus:
  • A longer film: 16 scenes, over 2 minutes
  • Every scene a video clip
  • Up to 16 affirmations
  • Your own photos in any scene

Create your film

One payment per film. No subscription. Secure checkout by Stripe.

How long is a film?

Standard: 90 seconds, ten scenes of nine seconds each. Premium: over 2 minutes with 16 scenes.

Is this a subscription?

No. You pay once per film.

Can I use my own photos?

Yes, with Premium you can add your own photo to any scene.

Can I download my film?

Yes. You can download it or share it with a private link.

How often should I watch my film?

Once a day, at the same moment, for example with your morning coffee. In a study on habits, linking a new habit to a fixed daily moment helped it stick. It took a median of 66 days to become automatic, and missing a single day did not matter (Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010).

Is there research behind this?

Yes, on mental imagery in general. In studies, imagining positive scenes lifted mood more than thinking about them in words, and imagining a best possible future for a few minutes a day raised optimism. Visionflick itself has not been studied, and it does not promise results.

Is Visionflick a manifestation tool?

Many people use it as part of their manifestation practice: a daily moment to see and hear their goals. We don’t claim that thoughts attract outcomes. What research does support is more down to earth: specific goals, reminders that name your own goal, and imagining the steps toward it can help people stick with their goals. Visionflick itself has not been studied.

Does it guarantee results?

No. Visionflick is a tool for daily visualization, not therapy or advice.

Begin your short morning ritual. Start with the areas that matter to you. Your storyboard is free.

What research says

Visionflick builds on well-studied findings about mental imagery and goals.

  • Pictures move us more than words. Imagining positive scenes lifted mood more than thinking about them in words. Holmes et al., Behavior Therapy, 2006 Holmes et al., Emotion, 2008
  • Pictures stay with you. We remember pictures better than words. Paivio & Csapo, Cognitive Psychology, 1973
  • A few minutes a day. Imagining your best possible future for five minutes a day raised optimism in studies. And in field studies, reminders that named a person’s own goal helped them stick to it. Generic reminders did not. Meevissen et al., J. Behav. 瑟尔。 过期。 Psychiatry, 2011 Carrillo et al., PLoS ONE, 2019 Karlan et al., Management Science, 2016
  • Imagining uses your visual brain. Imagining a scene uses many of the same brain systems as seeing it. Kosslyn et al., Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2001 Pearson, Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 2019
  • Rehearsing in your mind. Mental practice can improve your performance. Pascual-Leone et al., J. Neurophysiology, 1995 Toth et al., Psychology of Sport and Exercise, 2020
  • Be specific, and picture the steps. Specific goals lead to better performance than a vague “do your best”. And imagining the steps helped students more than imagining only the result. Locke & Latham, American Psychologist, 2002 Pham & Taylor, Pers. 苏克。 心理。 Bulletin, 1999

These studies looked at mental imagery and goals in general, not at Visionflick itself.

How often should I watch my film?

Once a day, at the same moment, for example with your morning coffee. In a study on habits, linking a new habit to a fixed daily moment helped it stick. It took a median of 66 days to become automatic, and missing a single day did not matter (Lally et al., European Journal of Social Psychology, 2010).

Is there research behind this?

Yes, on mental imagery in general. In studies, imagining positive scenes lifted mood more than thinking about them in words, and imagining a best possible future for a few minutes a day raised optimism. Visionflick itself has not been studied, and it does not promise results.

Is Visionflick a manifestation tool?

Many people use it as part of their manifestation practice: a daily moment to see and hear their goals. We don’t claim that thoughts attract outcomes. What research does support is more down to earth: specific goals, reminders that name your own goal, and imagining the steps toward it can help people stick with their goals. Visionflick itself has not been studied.

Does it guarantee results?

No. Visionflick is a tool for daily visualization, not therapy or advice.
